name: Twitch
tagline: Live-streaming community platform for gaming, IRL and creators
facts: ~$1.75B est. annual; not disclosed by Amazon
Long loss-making; 35% staff cut 2024 to chase profit
Shut South Korea service Feb 2024 over costs

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Empower communities to create together, live; a place to hang out with people who share your interests.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: The home of live: where creators build real-time communities, not passive audiences.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Monetise community, not views: subs, Bits, gifting and ads; extend reach via clips on TikTok, Shorts, Reels.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Live chat culture, emotes, raids, subscriber identity and gaming network effects built over 15 years.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Vertical and dual-format streaming, clips and Recaps feed for mobile discovery; cost discipline under Amazon.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Should Twitch chase short-form discovery or double down on long, live community where it is uniquely strong?

customers.who: Gamers, Gen Z, esports and IRL fans
customers.pain: Want real-time interaction and belonging, not passive watching
customers.why: Live chat, emotes, community rituals and favourite streamers live daily

customers.pain: Hard discovery, uneven income, competing revenue splits
customers.why: Built-in monetisation: subs, Bits, ads, Partner Plus 60/40 and 70/30 splits

customers.who: Game publishers, energy drinks, tech brands
customers.pain: Reach hard-to-target young male gaming audience
customers.why: Highly engaged live audience, sponsorship integrations, Amazon Ads stack

customers.pain: Want perks for games and streamers
customers.why: Free monthly Prime Gaming sub to support a streamer
Drops, category pages and co-streaming rights drive game discovery

rows.who_pays: Viewers ($4.99+) or Amazon via Prime Gaming
rows.how: Split 50/50 by default; 60/40 or 70/30 via Partner Plus
Pre/mid-rolls; streamers get share of ad revenue
Twitch keeps margin on Bits purchase; streamer gets $0.01 per Bit
Campaigns, Drops integrations, branded content deals

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: Estimated ~$1.75B/year split across subs, ads and Bits; Amazon does not disclose.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Most viewers never pay; a small core of subscribers and gifters funds creators.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: Live video bandwidth is costly; $1B+ paid to streamers yearly; high take on subs, thin ad CPMs.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: Mobile vertical live, clips for off-platform discovery, better ad tech, mid-tier creator retention.

bullets.label: Lesson
bullets.text: Strong community does not equal profit: serving costs and creator splits squeeze margins under parent scrutiny.

friction: New streamers struggle to be discovered
Long, frequent mid-roll ads frustrate viewers
Mobile app weaker than TikTok or YouTube
